title: Specification approval gate (foundational)
description: Generation starts only from an approved specification: a reviewed document naming the database's purpose, schema, and source material. The approval gate refuses ad-hoc generation requests without a spec, because unscoped generation produces unusable databases. Approved specs are versioned and linked to everything generated from them. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
spec = {'title': 'Index Structures DB', 'approved': True, 'version': '1.0'}
print('generation', 'APPROVED -> proceed' if spec['approved'] else 'BLOCKED: spec not approved')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Database Generator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Schema materialization into validators (foundational)
description: The spec's schema is materialized into executable validators: one predicate per field checking type, range, and format. Materialized validators run on every synthesized record before acceptance. A schema that cannot be materialized, such as one with contradictory constraints, fails the build early. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Database Generator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Record synthesis from source material (foundational)
description: Records are synthesized by combining source material excerpts with the schema's structure, deterministically from a seed so builds reproduce. Each record cites the source excerpts it drew on, preserving provenance through synthesis. Deterministic synthesis means the same spec and seed always build the same database. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import random
rng = random.Random(42)
sources = ['inverted index', 'hash table', 'btree']
recs = [{'id': f'r{i}', 'topic': rng.choice(sources)} for i in range(3)]
print('synthesized:', recs[0])
print('deterministic:', [r['topic'] for r in recs] == [r['topic'] for r in recs])
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Database Generator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-record validation: uniqueness and coverage (foundational)
description: The full synthesized set is validated together: identifiers unique, required categories covered, no exact-duplicate records. Cross-record checks catch problems invisible to per-record validation, like a build that generated the same record fifty times. Failures send the build back to synthesis with adjusted parameters. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
recs = [{'id': 'r1'}, {'id': 'r2'}, {'id': 'r1'}]
ids = [r['id'] for r in recs]
print('unique ids:', len(set(ids)) == len(ids), '| dupes:', len(ids) - len(set(ids)))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Database Generator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Database package assembly (foundational)
description: Validated records are assembled into the standard package: gzipped JSONL index, chunk files, generator script, and page scaffold. Assembly follows the same layout every database in the network uses, so generated databases slot into the archive without special handling. The package manifest records the spec version and seed used. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
